title: Evaluating Human Sensitivity to Gender Biased AI-Generated Content through Human Assessment of Google's Autocomplete Function
abstract: arXiv:2611.18371v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly present, but their effects on human users remain underexplored. We tested whether AI-attributed information influences views regarding gender-related statements, a domain where biases are pervasive. Spanish-speaking participants recruited through Prolific evaluated biased statements derived from Google's autocomplete function and human-authored, non-biased gender-related facts. Participants were either informed that some of the material was AI-generated or received no information about its origin. AI attribution did not affect reaction times or agreement judgments. This result suggests that AI-generated content does not automatically raise credibility concerns and may be evaluated with less scrutiny compared to human-produced content.

translated_title: 通过人工评估Google自动补全功能来评估人类对性别偏见AI生成内容的敏感度
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）日益普及，但其对人类用户的影响仍未得到充分探索。我们测试了AI来源标注是否会影响人们对性别相关陈述的看法，而性别是一个偏见普遍存在的领域。通过Prolific招募的西班牙语参与者评估了源自Google自动补全功能的偏见陈述，以及人类撰写的无偏见性别相关事实。参与者要么被告知部分材料是AI生成的，要么未获得关于其来源的任何信息。结果表明，AI来源标注并未影响参与者的反应时间或认同判断。这一结果提示，AI生成的内容并不会自动引发可信度方面的担忧，与人类创作的内容相比，人们可能以更少的审视来评估AI生成的内容。
tldr: 研究发现AI来源标注不会影响人们对性别相关陈述的反应时间与认同判断，表明人类评估AI生成内容时可能不如评估人类创作内容那样审慎。
en_tdlr: AI attribution does not affect reaction times or agreement judgments on gender-related statements, suggesting that people may evaluate AI-generated content with less scrutiny than human-produced content.
